subject: POC qualification: model shortlist, benchmarks, and quantization considerations
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Tara Nguyen <tara@medisphere.ai>, Alex Romero <alex.romero@medisphere.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Initial post-call recap + model shortlist for POC

Hi Tara / Alex — thanks again for a productive demo and the clarity on your throughput targets. Quick recap from today and a proposed shortlist for the 2-week pilot so we can validate both quality and unit-cost impact. Attaching the raw microbenchmarks we ran on similar doc-summarization prompts.

Key inputs from your side:
- Latency SLO: 300ms p95 for single-request summarization path (avg doc length ~1.5k tokens)
- Target throughput: 40 reqs/min sustained, burst to 120
- Quality tolerance: safe up to ~2% absolute drop on rouge/accuracy vs current baseline (but we'd like to measure perception on a small holdout set)
- Security: must pass SOC2 evidence check and be deployable in your VPC for prod

Proposed model shortlist (for evaluation):
1) Llama-3-70B-8k (FP16 baseline) — expect best-isomorphic quality, heavier latency/cost. Good for fidelity-sensitive routes.
2) Redstone-XXL-13B (AWQ 4-bit candidate) — moderate fidelity drop, much lower cost and better throughput on NVIDIA A100/RTX8000.
3) OpenInf-30B (GPTQ 4-bit) — middle ground: strong generative quality with aggressive quantization maturity.

Quantization/throughput knobs we recommend testing:
- AWQ 4-bit (fast inference, typically +2–3x throughput vs fp16; watch for name-entity hallucinations in summarization)
- GPTQ 4-bit fallback (safer in some layers; often slightly higher latency than AWQ at same precision)
- FP8 experimental path (promising on some kernels; may require conservative rollout)

Attached: medisphere-benchmark-results.csv (microbenchmarks on your prompt subset). Also sharing a working promptset (promptset-v1.txt) that mirrors the holdout you described.

Ask / next steps:
- Can you confirm the 2-week pilot window and which route (summarization vs extraction) you want prioritized?
- Please share any additional holdout prompt IDs for quality gating.
- I'll loop in Aditya to run an overnight AWQ vs GPTQ pass and produce a quick throughput/quality delta table by Friday EOD.

Thanks — looking forward to validating the tradeoffs.

Best,
Markus
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Markus — this is great, appreciate the clear shortlist. A few clarifications from our side:

- We can confirm a 2-week pilot starting Monday 3/18. Prioritize the summarization route first (that’s the higher-risk customer-facing flow).
- The holdout set: attached are three prompt IDs and expected outputs (separate file uploaded to your Drive link). We want human-judged fidelity > 95% of baseline; if automatic metrics drop >2% we still might accept if human scores hold, but would like early flags.

I'll get the legal SOW contact ready (we may need a short addendum for private VPC deploy later).

—tara

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Medisphere — AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 trade summary and quick runs

Team — following up on the pilot kickoff on Monday. Tara asked for concise throughput and cost deltas plus a quick quality delta table against their holdout. I ran a fast pass last night and left notes in the Drive folder. Summary below (very terse):

Test setup:
- Hardware: 2x A100-80GB (dedicated test pool), sequence len median 1.5k, batch simulated to match 40 rpm
- Promptset: promptset-v1.txt (see Drive)

Preliminary results (median/approx):
- Llama-3-70B (FP16): p95 latency ~480ms, throughput ~18 rpm, quality baseline = 100% on auto metric
- Redstone-XXL-13B (AWQ 4-bit): p95 latency ~220ms, throughput ~58 rpm, auto-metric delta ~ -1.8% vs baseline
- OpenInf-30B (GPTQ 4-bit): p95 latency ~260ms, throughput ~45 rpm, auto-metric delta ~ -1.1% vs baseline
- FP8 path (experimental on Llama-3-70B): p95 ~300ms (optimized kernels only), throughput ~35 rpm, auto-metric delta ~ -0.9% but unstable on certain token sequences

Interpretation / recommendation:
- If the hard constraint is 300ms p95 and 40 rpm, AWQ on Redstone-XXL-13B hits both comfortably but shows ~1.8% auto-metric drop; we should surface two things to the customer: (1) human-eval delta often smaller than auto-metric; (2) we can mitigate entity hallucinations with prompt tuning + caching.
- GPTQ 4-bit (OpenInf-30B) is more conservative on quality and still meets throughput targets with less aggressive quantization.
- FP8 is promising but requires a cautious A/B rollout: kernel availability varies by infra and we should not recommend FP8 for the first pilot week.

Operational notes for Redwood Dedicated config:
- Start with concurrency cap = 6 per-GPU, max_batch_size = 32, and autoscale headroom of 30% to absorb bursts (these numbers based on the above latencies)
- Enable prefix KV caching for repeated-document summarization (customer has repeated paragraph patterns)
- Add a low-cost canary route pinned to Llama-3-70B-FP16 for fallback when auto-metric drift > 2.5%

Aditya — can you produce a one-sheet (pdf) summarizing the above numbers and include cost-per-1M tokens for AWQ vs GPTQ (on A100) by EOD tomorrow? I attached a rough draft (redwood-quant-tradeoff.pdf) and the raw CSV.

Thanks,
Markus

Hi Tara / Alex — quick consolidated note before kickoff on Monday. We ran an overnight AWQ/GPTQ sweep and attached a short one-sheet with cost deltas. Key items and concrete next steps: 

1) Pilot plan (week 1):
- Route A (default): Redstone-XXL-13B @ AWQ-4 — expected to meet 300ms p95 and 40 rpm per-region.
- Route B (canary/fallback): OpenInf-30B @ GPTQ-4 — a conservative quality-first path.
- Guardrail: if auto-metric drift > 2.5% vs baseline for > 5 consecutive batches, traffic auto-fails over to Route B.

2) Deliverables by Redwood before Monday:
- promptset-v1.txt (attached) mapped to your holdout IDs
- medisphere-benchmark-results.csv (raw microbenchmarks)
- redwood-quant-tradeoff.pdf (one-sheet with cost per 1M tokens and throughput table)

- Confirm acceptance criteria for human-eval gating (we can run a quick human review on a 200-sample batch mid-week)
- Legal point of contact for the SOW addendum (we'll need contact for a potential VPC deployment)

If that all looks good, we’ll spin up the dedicated pool and smoke-test the AWQ route first thing Monday morning. I’ve CC’d Aditya and Lauren for ops and legal handoff.

Thanks — excited to get this running.

Best,
Markus
